status: Design contract only; this does not activate a new profile slot or award currency.
presentation: Old-school top-down RPG scene presentation; the player's action is composing the rhythm puzzle answer.
runRules: A new playthrough starts with the nine authored tiles, one of each kind. Inventory carries between puzzles in that playthrough.
Save the exact ordered note-kind recipe for each committed answer. A duration total or door ID cannot reconstruct the stock or route.
The active answer prefix deterministically derives scene, inventory, current-run flags and already-credited stage packs from chapter content.
An accepted answer consumes its actual tiles. Entry to a later puzzle stage credits exactly its three authored tiles once. Terminal entry credits no tiles.
Undo/revisit replays a shorter answer prefix, restoring stock, flags and stage receipts together. The new answer replaces the abandoned continuation; future stock or flags never travel backward.
Rendering, reload, retry and revisiting a checkpoint do not issue another pack. Fixed authored packs require no random seed or reroll mechanic.
Chapter content is versioned. A future incompatible rule change must migrate or restart the current run while preserving bounded discovery records.
Do not merge two divergent active runs during synchronization. Discovery sets may merge by union independently of the chosen active run.

collection.unknownOutcomes: Player journal conceals undiscovered names and exact solutions. The developer's design explorer deliberately reveals them.
collection.monotonic: Discovered outcomes and causes remain found after undo/restart. Permanent discoveries never satisfy a current-run story promise.
collection.causeRules: Record all applicable cause tags for the selected dead-end family. A wrong door and a missing promise may both be true; cause tags are journal detail rather than extra endings.

efficiency.metric: Consumed note tiles in a successful completed answer sequence. Physical board manipulation costs require a separate definition when layouts are implemented.
efficiency.comparison: Compare a result with the verified minimum for that same outcome. A shorter early dead end is never a better success score.
efficiency.bestByOutcome: Store only completed, replay-verified records keyed by the authored outcome ID. Undoing before an outcome is not a completion.

rewards.amounts: Not yet assigned; changing cosmetic reward amounts does not alter the verified puzzle resource model.
rewards.currency: Puzzle note blocks are consumable inventory. Arcade Notes are a separate wallet currency; leftover blocks do not automatically convert into Notes.
rewards.authority: An active arcade host validates the bounded answer log and derives the terminal ID and reward amount from authored content.
rewards.onceOnly: First discovery and later efficiency milestones use stable receipts. Replays, undo and reset never create a new receipt for the same milestone.
rewards.deltaUpgrade: A first optimal finish claims the base reward and efficiency delta once; improving a prior finish claims only the missing delta.
rewards.deadEnds: Journal discovery and explanatory feedback. A nonzero Notes reward for dead ends is not part of this design.
rewards.implementation: Reuse the existing Notes wallet and achievement journals. Bound the full receipt ID to 100 characters; never include a run ID, deployment version or retry counter.

futureIntegration.client: Add an optional scoped story record to classroom-profile-data.js capture/apply/validation and backup handling.
futureIntegration.server: A synchronized implementation also needs coordinated optional DTO rules for teacher-player and student-profile state in docs/firebase-google-classroom.rules.json.
futureIntegration.compatibility: Older profiles and saved maps remain valid with the new optional record absent.
futureIntegration.standalone: Keep standalone guest progress isolated. A bare game page must not construct a shared Notes wallet with an incomplete ownership catalog.
